Evidence read at origin/main 6ebc43bd8; not reproduced on a live project.\\n\\nShape: one task, one small pull request, not stacked. Nothing else depends on it.\\n\\nThe defect, in src/Hall9k.Daemon/AutoPrReview/AutoPrReviewEngine.cs:\\n- ConcludeWithdrawnAsync (line 1668) builds stillRequested from pull request numbers alone (line 1672).\\n- Its watched-task query filters on the project, the login, the type and the state, never on a repository (lines 1675-1680).\\n- It reads ExternalReference.Key, which is the bare number (ExternalReference.cs, Key), and compares only that (lines 1698-1702). The reference itself is the canonical owner/repo#N, and the repository half is discarded.\\n- ConcludeOneAsync then asks the swept repository\\u0027s timeline about that number (lines 1734-1736), so a removal on a different pull request can stand as proof, and the task is recalled and, before dispatch, abandoned (lines 1805-1837).\\n\\nThe sibling already has the right shape: ForgetWithdrawnObservationsAsync (line 1154) is scoped to the repository case-insensitively (line 1165), and its doc comment (lines 1125-1137) gives this very reason: a row recorded when the project pointed at a different repository must not be judged by a search that never covered it. GitHubPullRequestReference.TryParseCanonical splits a stored reference back into repository and number.\\n\\nReachability: latent. ProjectRegistered is the only event that writes RepositoryUrl, so a project with a recorded URL always sweeps one repository. The route in is a project with no recorded URL, where the sweep falls back to gh repo view (lines 730-731), re-pointed with h9k project set --repo at a clone of a different repository. RunLauncher.cs:1159-1162 names the same route. The Solutions work keeps one repository per project, so it does not widen this.\\n\\nCompare case-insensitively: the sweep\\u0027s repository comes from the project\\u0027s URL, while a reference carries GitHub\\u0027s own casing (lines 1195-1200 explain why they can differ).\\n\\nFor the walk: a repository rename or transfer would leave older references under the old name. Under this fix they are skipped, which costs a missed recall rather than a wrongly abandoned task; the file\\u0027s own comment at lines 1119-1121 prefers that pr review refuses a pull request from a repository other than its project\\u0027s own before it records or checks out anything, so a reviewer is never handed one pull request\\u0027s briefing over another pull request\\u0027s code.\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022h9k pr review with an owner/repo#N or a URL naming a repository other than the project\\u0027s exits non-zero and says why on stderr, naming both repositories and that reviewing it needs a project registered against that repository.\u0022,\u0022After that refusal nothing has changed: no task, claim, run, worktree or tracking ref was created. This holds with --no-worktree, with --since-my-review, and when a live task already holds the foreign pull request.\u0022,\u0022A number, a shorthand or a URL naming the project\\u0027s own repository opens a lap as it does today, including when the repository\\u0027s letter casing differs from the project\\u0027s recorded URL.\u0022,\u0022When neither the project\\u0027s recorded URL nor gh repo view can name the project\\u0027s repository, the lap proceeds, matching the daemon\\u0027s guard.\u0022,\u0022Automated tests cover the first three criteria through the command\\u0027s scripted gh and worktree seams, without touching real git or GitHub.\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Hand-off from idea f8212260\\u0027s discovery (its workspace findings.md:185-187), where it was inferred. Settled here by reading the code at origin/main 6ebc43bd8: the daemon\\u0027s guard exists and the command has none. Not run live.\\n\\nShape: one task, one small pull request, not stacked. 71b8826c (a draft about a missing archived-project check in the same method) touches the same area and is an independent defect, so neither blocks the other.\\n\\nThe daemon refuses this case at both of its checkout sites, before any fetch: src/Hall9k.Daemon/Execution/RunLauncher.cs:243-271 and 1156-1173. Its comment states the hazard: the checkout fetches from the project\\u0027s own origin, so a pull request from a different repository either silently checks out whatever pull request shares that number, or fails with an unhelpful missing-ref error.\\n\\nThe command has no such check, in src/Hall9k.Cli/Commands/PullRequestReviewCommand.cs:\\n- The argument accepts owner/repo#N and URLs (help text, lines 65-70), and GitHubPullRequestSurface.cs:151-158 passes that repository to gh pr view --repo.\\n- RunAsync goes straight from the read (lines 139-141) to minting the reference (line 143), then to the adopt and attach arms (lines 148-171). No line compares pullRequest.Repository with the project\\u0027s repository.\\n- Both checkout sites cut by number from project.RepositoryPath (lines 620-621 and 854-856). GitWorktreeManager.cs:209-210 fetches refs/pull/N/head from origin.\\n- The command\\u0027s PrReviewWorktreeRequest passes no head commit, unlike RunLauncher.cs:1193, so nothing notices the mismatch.\\n\\nThe result is a briefing about one pull request over a checkout of another, which is worse than a failure because it reads as a normal lap.\\n\\nPlace the check before the two arms so that it covers adoption and attachment alike. It also applies under --no-worktree, where there is no wrong checkout but the lap would still put a review task on the wrong project\\u0027s board, the hazard the doc comment at lines 239-242 names.\\n\\nRunLauncher.OwnerRepoFrom is internal to the daemon (RunLauncher.cs:2513) and the CLI cannot reach it. PullRequestUrls.RepositoryFrom (Hall9k.Connectors, PullRequestUrls.cs:53) is the same shape and is reachable from both; GitHubWorkItemProvider.TryObserveRepositoryHostAsync is the shared fallback.\\n\\nRunAsync already takes its gh and git seams as parameters for tests. tests/Hall9k.Tests/Integration/ReviewLapTests.cs has no case for from idea f8212260\\u0027s discovery (its workspace findings.md:187, which cites docs/scope.md:1587; the line is 1691 at origin/main 6ebc43bd8).\\n\\nShape: one task, one small pull request, not stacked.\\n\\nWhat exists. The platform ships no create-pr skill: it is absent from the repository\\u0027s .claude/skills, from the install\\u0027s ~/.hall9k/skills, and from src (git grep finds it only in the five files named below). The hall9k project home does carry one, a plain directory at skills/create-pr dated 2026-09-14 rather than a link into the install, so it is project-specific in the tier AGENTS.md describes (\\u0022project-specific skills beside the links\\u0022). The sentence \\u0022there is deliberately no create-pr skill\\u0022 is therefore too broad: it is true of the platform and false of this home.\\n\\nFour sites carry the same sentence, and fixing one would leave three stale: AGENTS.md:137, ORCHESTRATOR-WINDOW.md:467, docs/concepts.md:1045 and docs/scope.md:1691. backlog/01-repo-skills.md:16 is a historical instruction and stays as it is.\\n\\nThe rule itself does not change: the daemon opens pull requests (PullRequestOpener) and agents do not.\\n\\nThe type is chore rather than content because the project\\u0027s non-executable-path set excludes AGENTS.md, so a content task would be refused at the gates over that one line (h9k project show hall9k).\\n\\nOut of scope, for the walk if at all: whether the hall9k home should keep its create-pr skill, given that rule.\u0022,\u0022Constraints\u0022:null,\u0022ExternalReference\u0022:null,\u0022AddedAt\u0022:\u00222026-10-30T12:29:55.128337\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022AddedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022Model\u0022:\u0022\u0022,\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:[],\u0022StartsAsDraft\u0022:true,\u0022SourceIdeaId\u0022:null,\u0022EpicId\u0022:null,\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:null,\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:null,\u0022PreApproved\u0022:false,\u0022Origin\u0022:null,\u0022PreApproval\u0022:\u0022Off\u0022,\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:null,\u0022SecondaryExternalReference\u0022:null,\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:null,\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:null,\u0022InitialScope\u0022:\u0022Fleet\u0022}","originEventId":"5ac15a5d-717d-487e-95c0-20912cec2255","originSequence":145474,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-10-30T12:29:55.164512+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"}]
